briefs.headline: Palmer is suspended for Wednesday's cup trip to Liverpool
briefs.summary: Cole Palmer's first red card as a senior player, a second yellow for a late tackle on Conor Gallagher in the 80th minute of Saturday's home loss to Tottenham, carries an automatic one-match ban that falls on Chelsea's Carabao Cup fourth-round match at Anfield on Wednesday at 4 p.m. ET, so Palmer will be available for Manchester United's visit to Stamford Bridge on Saturday unless the suspension is extended. The dismissal was Chelsea's 100th in the Premier League, not counting rescinded cards; only Everton (113) and Arsenal (110) have more. Chelsea's players and staff were sent off 11 times last season, the most in the league, with Tottenham next on five. Palmer had been booked in the 70th for pushing his midriff into Mateus Fernandes' face as the midfielder lay on the ground. Chelsea dropped to 5th on Sunday when Liverpool, Wednesday's opponent, beat Brighton.

briefs.headline: Liverpool beat Brighton 2-0 for a first home league win under Iraola
briefs.summary: Liverpool scored twice in the first 21 minutes at Anfield on Sunday and won 2-0, their fourth straight victory in all competitions and their first home Premier League win since beating Crystal Palace in April. Florian Wirtz's 17th-minute shot went in off Pascal Gross for an own goal from Ronald Araujo's cross, and Alexander Isak turned in Bradley Barcola's cross from the right of the six-yard box in the 21st, his sixth goal in seven league appearances. Brighton had 64.4 percent of possession and 17 shots to 13 but put one on target; Yasin Ayari hit the post in the first half. Wirtz went off injured in the 65th minute after treatment at the hour mark. Fabian Hurzeler said "there was one team who really tried to create"; Andoni Iraola said "the key was how we started." Liverpool rise to 4th on 15 points and host Chelsea in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday at 4 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Burrow throws 4 TD passes as Bengals erase 13-0 deficit to beat Ravens 35-13
briefs.summary: Cincinnati was outgained 258 yards to 59 in the first half in Baltimore on Sunday and trailed 13-0, then scored touchdowns on its first five possessions after halftime and won 35-13 before 70,464 at M&T Bank Stadium. Joe Burrow went 22 of 30 for 292 yards and touchdown passes of 6 yards to Mike Gesicki, 13 to Tee Higgins, 2 to Ja'Marr Chase and 16 to Drew Sample; Samaje Perine ran in from the 1. Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards, all after halftime. Chase said he screamed at the offense at halftime that "somebody's got to make a play for us." Lamar Jackson missed a third straight game with his ankle injury; Tyler Huntley threw for 298 yards. Baltimore became the third team in NFL history to lead by 13 or more at the half and lose by 20 or more, per ESPN Research. The Bengals, 4-2 and third in the AFC North, host Tennessee on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Browns beat Titans 27-24 on Szmyt's field goal as time expires
briefs.summary: Deshaun Watson hit Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards to set up Andre Szmyt's 32-yard field goal on the final play, and Cleveland won 27-24 in Nashville, Tennessee, on Sunday for a fifth win in six games. Watson, who led his fifth fourth-quarter winning drive of the season, completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards and ran 9 yards for the touchdown that put Cleveland up 24-17 with 4:34 left; Tony Pollard's third touchdown run, with 58 seconds remaining, tied it. Quinshon Judkins, back from an ankle injury, ran for 96 yards and two scores, and rookie KC Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards; Titans coach Robert Saleh said officials appeared to miss a false start on the Fannin play. Separately, Maliek Collins' agent told ESPN on Sunday that the defensive tackle agreed to a two-year, $30 million extension with $23 million guaranteed. The Browns, 5-2 and tied atop the AFC North with Pittsburgh, visit the Steelers on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Pulisic, McKennie and Weah all score on the same Sunday in Europe
briefs.summary: Christian Pulisic opened the scoring in the sixth minute as AC Milan beat Udinese 2-0 in Serie A on Sunday, controlling Luka Modric's lofted free kick and sliding the ball past Maduka Okoye; Omari Hutchinson, on loan from Nottingham Forest, added his first Milan goal in the 65th after Okoye spilled a shot. Milan, beaten 3-0 at Bournemouth in the Europa League on Thursday, have 10 points from their last 12 in the league and climbed to fourth. U.S. teammates Weston McKennie and Timothy Weah also scored Sunday in wins for Juventus and Marseille. The national team next plays Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal first leg in Miami on Nov. 14.

briefs.headline: Brewers send Gasser against Peralta in World Series Game 3 at Tropicana Field
briefs.summary: Milwaukee, two games up after winning both at home, opens the Tampa Bay leg of the World Series on Monday at 8 p.m. ET at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida, with Robert Gasser starting for the Brewers against Freddy Peralta for the Rays, MLB.com's schedule listed. Sunday was a travel day with no game. Tampa Bay has to win four of the next five to take the Series.

briefs.headline: Lions beat Packers 20-17 on a last-play kick after Campbell's fourth-down gamble
briefs.summary: Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal as time expired Sunday in Detroit after Dan Campbell went for it on fourth-and-1 from his own 24 with under five minutes left and Jahmyr Gibbs was stopped for no gain. Green Bay got nothing from the gift: Jordan Love's pass hit Josh Jacobs' hands and fell incomplete in the end zone, and rookie Trey Smack had a 35-yard try partly blocked after missing from 26 in the first half, the first kicker since 2019 to miss twice from 35 yards or closer in one game. Brian Branch intercepted in his first game since tearing his Achilles tendon in December. Detroit is 4-2 and third in the NFC North behind Minnesota (6-0) and Chicago (5-2) and hosts the Vikings next Sunday; the Packers are 4-3 and last in a division where all four teams have winning records.

briefs.headline: Falcons force four turnovers to hand the 49ers their first loss 29-20
briefs.summary: Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes, to Nick Muse, Kyle Pitts and Drake London, and Atlanta scored 13 points off four San Francisco turnovers Sunday, the 49ers having given the ball away six times in their first six games. Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels intercepted Brock Purdy with 2:34 left and recovered a George Kittle fumble inside the final minute; a replay review took away a 23-yard Purdy touchdown pass to Jordan Watkins. Christian McCaffrey missed much of the first half with a thigh injury and finished with seven carries. San Francisco is 6-1 and Atlanta 3-4. Kansas City also lost its unbeaten record Sunday night in Seattle, held to a field goal and 213 yards as Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards; the Chiefs are 5-1 and Minnesota is the last undefeated team.

briefs.headline: Bournemouth beats Manchester United 3-0 as Carrick benches Fernandes
briefs.summary: Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson scored at Old Trafford on Sunday after Michael Carrick left Bruno Fernandes out of the squad for the match and did not use him from the bench, days after the captain criticized the team's tactics following a 4-1 Champions League loss at Como. "It's a tough situation. I won't hide from it. What's next? I really don't know," Carrick told Sky Sports. United has one win in eight league matches and sits 16th on seven points; Manchester City and Arsenal lead on 21 after eight rounds, with Brighton third on 16. Newcastle won 2-0 at Crystal Palace and Sunderland stayed bottom on five points after a scoreless draw with Leeds.

briefs.headline: Doncic scores 52 in Utah as six teams finish the NBA's opening week unbeaten
briefs.summary: Luka Doncic hit eight 3-pointers and scored 52 points, the league's first 50-point game of the season, with 10 assists, and the Lakers erased an 18-point deficit to beat the Jazz 132 to 123 in Salt Lake City on Sunday. Detroit, playing its first game without center Jalen Duren, out at least two weeks with a strained hamstring, led wire to wire and beat Philadelphia 106 to 93 behind Cade Cunningham's 26, handing the 76ers their first loss with Joel Embiid resting. The Pistons, Lakers, Thunder, Timberwolves, Grizzlies and Rockets are unbeaten at three wins apiece, and Portland has won both of its games. The Knicks, Bucks, Nets and Heat are winless after three in the East, as are the Warriors, Kings and Pelicans in the West.

briefs.headline: Canadiens beat Jets 2-1 outdoors in Winnipeg's first game since the Hellebuyck trade
briefs.summary: Jacob Fowler made 33 saves and Lane Hutson and Kaiden Guhle scored as Montreal won the NHL Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium on Sunday night, Fowler's fifth straight winning start; Isak Rosen scored for Winnipeg with 4:46 left. It was the Jets' first game since sending goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey on Friday, and Dawson Mercer, the centerpiece of the return, played 15:22. Montreal is 6-3-2 and Winnipeg 4-4-3. Elsewhere Sunday, Quinn Hughes had a goal and an assist in his first game back in Vancouver as Minnesota beat the Canucks, who are 2-10-1.

briefs.headline: Ohio State rises to No. 2 and BYU drops to No. 8 as Miami stays atop the AP poll
briefs.summary: The AP Top 25 released Sunday kept unbeaten Miami at No. 1 and moved one-loss Ohio State up one spot to No. 2 after UCF's double-overtime win dropped BYU six places to eighth. Georgia rose to No. 3, Indiana to No. 4 and Notre Dame slipped to fifth; unbeaten Utah climbed four spots to sixth and unbeaten UCLA is seventh. Texas jumped eight places to No. 11 and Ole Miss fell five to 12th after Saturday's losses by Texas Tech and Tennessee reshuffled the top half of the poll.

briefs.headline: Kyushu banzuke keeps Onosato and Hoshoryu as yokozuna, lifts Aonishiki to top ozeki
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association released the banzuke (rankings) Monday for the Kyushu basho (tournament), which opens Nov. 8 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center, 13 days out. Onosato, 26, the September champion with 12 wins in 15 bouts, is East yokozuna (grand champion) and Hoshoryu, 27, who had right knee surgery after July and missed all of September, remains West yokozuna; Nikkan Sports reported he joined the autumn tour partway through and that whether he competes is still being watched, with no kyujo (absence) announced. Aonishiki, 22, runner-up with 11 wins, moves to East ozeki (champion) No. 1 ahead of Kotozakura and Kirishima. Fujinokawa and Atamifuji are the sekiwake (junior champions); Minoumi, 33, becomes the first Okinawa-born rikishi (wrestler) to reach komusubi (the lowest titled rank), and Tamawashi, 41, returns to the top division as the oldest wrestler to regain a top-division rank since the start of the Showa era in 1926.

prime.item: Day 12. Proclamation SF-1-2026, issued Oct. 2 by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler, made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation; as Thursday's desk read it, the limit for unlicensed persons and harvesters taking oysters for personal consumption is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, with a three-inch minimum shell length, no taking between sunset and sunrise, and the oyster sanctuaries of rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 closed. The division's proclamations index, pages 0 and 1 read at 5:50 a.m. this morning, lists SF-1-2026 as issued Oct. 2 and carries no later shellfish proclamation. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:49 a.m., still carries the Sept. 2 table with its oyster row reading season closed, while its footnote (I) reads that oyster season is Oct. 15 to March 31 unless closed earlier by proclamation; the proclamation controls. The proclamation PDF itself was not re-opened today. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:49 a.m. and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, with the footnote that it is unlawful to possess red drum over 27 inches or to gig, spear or gaff them. The proclamations index, pages 0 and 1 read at 5:50 a.m., carries no 2026 recreational red drum proclamation; the newest proclamation listed is FF-47-2026 of Friday, Oct. 23, a commercial flounder order, and nothing is listed as issued Oct. 24, 25 or 26. The reference calendar's October pattern has red drum running and its November pattern leads with them. The reference seasonal calendar, not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Oct. 1, is 24.9 days old this morning and past the 21-day gate, and no November report has posted.

waters.reading: 112 cfs, 1.70 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on discharge and on stage against 148 cfs and 1.87 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Down 16 cfs and 0.08 feet on the day against the USGS trace's 128 cfs and 1.78 feet at 5:15 a.m. Sunday, Sunday's edition reading, a ninth straight falling morning with the recession still slowing: 208 at 5:15 Thursday and 174 at 6 a.m. Friday as Sunday's edition carried them, 148 Saturday, 128 Sunday and 112 this morning (34, 26, 20, 16), and the trace shows no rain bump overnight, a steady slide from 116 at midnight to 112 at 5:15. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, "112 cfs - prime wading water.", its band for 100 to 200 cfs, and the river sits 12 cfs above the floor of it; another two or three mornings at this rate puts it under 100. The fetcher's 148 cfs and 1.87 feet 24h_ago fields match the trace's Saturday 4:30 to 7 a.m. points, about 48 hours old, so the 36-cfs drop they imply is two days' worth; the falling flags are right. At 112 and clear after nine days of recession the Williams is the long-leader, small-fly problem the desk's instructions describe, and more so than Sunday: the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure are wadeable across at this flow, the pockets are thin, and the fish in the plunge-pool tail-outs see the angler and the line before the fly. Caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage the file records, so a 12-foot leader to 6X or 7X with a size 18 caddis pupa or pheasant tail under a small yarn indicator, or a size 16 elk-hair caddis with a size 18 dropper, fished from downstream up the seams and the plunge-pool tail-outs in the afternoon when the water is warmest; a size 8 to 10 weighted stonefly only in the deepest plunge pools, where the depth hides the approach; and the sculpin pattern, olive or black, swung under the undercut banks at first and last light, the only hours low clear water does not work against it. The Williams River in Pocahontas and Webster counties is on WVDNR's fall trout stocking schedule, code F in the 2026 Fishing Regulations Summary as Thursday's desk read it, one stocking each week for two weeks beginning the third Monday of October, which was Oct. 19; the second week begins today. WVDNR posts stockings by the end of each business day; its fish-stocking page, opened at 5:47 this morning, fills its stocked-waters table by script from a spreadsheet this desk did not read, and the trout-stocking address redirected to an old release on Bear Rock Lakes WMA in the Northern Panhandle, so no delivery to the Williams, the Cranberry or the Summersville tailwater is confirmed this morning. The fetcher carries no Williams water temperature, so none is printed.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.05 feet at 5 a.m., rising against 24.59 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.1 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the pool rising, up 0.46 against its 24.59 comparison point; against the USGS trace's 24.43 at 5 a.m. Sunday, Sunday's edition reading, the gauge is up 0.62 on the day, well outside the fetcher's 0.25-foot steady band, so the rising flag holds either way. The trace shows the pool came off to 24.21 at noon Sunday, its low of the day, and rose 0.84 overnight to this morning's 25.05, the highest reading since Thursday's 24.99, with Huntington below the dam coming up 0.50 in the same hours, which is the pool being brought up, not a river in flood; the Williams above showed no rain overnight. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 25.1 the gauge is 1.9 feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27 feet. A pool coming up a half foot or more overnight on structure puts current on the wing dams and moves the bait, and at normal pool the river fishes that structure and the current it makes, not the slack: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap where the current breaks; a half-ounce blade bait or a jigging spoon on the lock wall's deep edge for the sauger, which the cooling water and last night's full moon favor after dark; crawfish are the third forage the file records, so a crawfish-colored jig in the riprap for the smallmouth; and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark, with the rising water putting them on the move. The Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no lake elevation or release figure is printed.

waters.working: The fetcher reads the gauge steady, up 0.08 against its 26.26 comparison point, and the flag holds on the day: against the USGS trace's 26.47 at 5 a.m. Sunday, Sunday's edition reading, the gauge is down 0.13, inside the fetcher's 0.25-foot steady band. The trace shows it fell to 25.84 at 4:45 p.m. Sunday, its low of the day, and came up 0.50 overnight to this morning's 26.34, with Point Pleasant above the dam up 0.84 over the same hours, the signature of the dam passing water, though the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no release figure is printed. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 26.3 the gauge is seven-tenths of a foot under the 27-foot line between that band and up and pushing, an eighth normal-pool morning. A pool coming up overnight below the dam puts current on the structure, which is where the fish hold: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam rather than the eddy behind it; a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head along the riprap points in low light; a black-and-blue jig for the smallmouth and the drum in the rock; cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark; and the lock wall from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids while the gates are passing water.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 2:47 AM at 0.2 ft, high 8:52 AM at 4.6 ft, low 3:39 PM at 0.5 ft, high 9:11 PM at 3.7 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 1:18 AM at -0.1 ft, high 7:49 AM at 6.0 ft, low 2:11 PM at -0.0 ft, high 8:08 PM at 4.6 ft. Water 63.7F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon full, 100% lit, 15.0 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 8:52 AM and 9:11 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Full moon, the morning after: the fetcher's file carries the moon as full, 100 percent lit and 15.0 days old, the full having fallen at 04:12 UT today, 12:12 a.m. ET, by the U.S. Naval Observatory table Wednesday's edition cited, not re-queried today, and the spring tides are at their peak. The sound at Hampstead bottomed at 0.2 feet at 2:47 a.m., and is on its flood at press time, filling 4.4 feet to a 4.6-foot high at 8:52 a.m., the biggest swing and the highest water of the month's table so far, two-tenths above Sunday's 4.4; it drains 4.1 feet to a 0.5-foot low at 3:39 p.m., fills 3.2 feet to a 3.7-foot high at 9:11 p.m. and drains toward Tuesday's early low, which falls outside today's table. All four sound events land inside Monday; nothing carries a spillover tag today. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 1:18 a.m. at -0.1, high 7:49 a.m. at 6.0, low 2:11 p.m. at -0.0, high 8:08 p.m. at 4.6, a 6.1-foot flood against Sunday's 5.6. Today's lags from the two tables are 63 and 63 minutes on the highs and 89 and 88 minutes on the lows; the lows again lag longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the ebb at the crew's spot past what a flat offset would give. NWS Wilmington has the beach and the water covered for a second morning, a step down from Sunday's gale: a Coastal Flood Advisory for Coastal Pender County, issued 2:29 a.m., until 10 a.m., up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways, low-lying roads along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks named for minor flooding, which lands on the 8:52 a.m. sound high; a Rip Current Statement for Coastal Pender, issued 2:29 a.m., a High Rip Current Risk from 6 a.m. through 8 p.m. with a strong north-to-south longshore current; and a Small Craft Advisory on the coastal waters out 20 nautical miles, issued 11:02 p.m. Sunday, until 1 a.m. Tuesday, northeast winds 20 to 30 knots and seas 5 to 8 feet, conditions the service says will be hazardous to small craft; Sunday's Gale Warning has expired. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 63.7 degrees at 5:30 a.m., unchanged from Sunday's edition; the fetcher's file gives no reading at Topsail itself. What is running is the reference seasonal calendar, labeled as such and not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, is 24.9 days old this morning and past the paper's 21-day gate, the feed still carried it as its newest item at 5:47 a.m., and no November report has posted. The calendar's October pattern is spot at the peak of the run, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum; its November pattern, a week away, is red drum, speckled trout at their prime, bluefish, spot, sea mullet and blow toads, and a Beaufort thermometer holding under 64 is the cool-down that pattern turns on. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem, and the weather again sets the water: the surf and the piers are under the High Rip Current Risk and the ocean under the Small Craft Advisory with a northeast wind of 20 to 30 knots still on the beach, and the inlet on a full-moon ebb against that wind is the hardest current of the month, so the oceanfront and the inlet are not the day's water and the sound inside the island is. The sound flood runs to 8:52 a.m. with 4.6 feet over the grass and up the dock pilings, the flooded-high stage where the drum push into the grass and the dock flats, finger mullet and shrimp the forage the file records, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the flooded grass edges and down the dock lines on the top of the flood, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead as the bars go under. The ebb from 8:52 a.m. to 3:39 p.m. is the day's working window, 6 hours 47 minutes of falling water on the peak spring tide, 4.1 feet of water and the bait in it pulled out of the marsh; the red drum stage, the last of the fall, is roughly 1:40 to 3:40 p.m., in full daylight, a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the ICWW channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low, and with the northeast wind still on the water the lee shorelines and the creek mouths on the mainland side are where it can be cast. For spot, the calendar's October peak, a two-hook bottom rig with bloodworm or shrimp bits on the channel edges on the moving water either side of the 3:39 p.m. low. The flood from 3:39 to 9:11 p.m. covers the oyster bars and grass edges again, the same spoon and paddletail program, and dusk falls on the middle of the flood, the trout window the calendar is a week from calling prime: a Spook Jr. or a suspending twitch bait walked over the deeper grass edges and the dock lights in the last hour of light, then a live shrimp under a slip cork in the deeper holes, 15 to 20 feet, on the first of the evening ebb after 9:11 p.m. under a full moon that will light the water. Slack at 8:52 a.m., 3:39 p.m. and 9:11 p.m. is dead water, and on a spring tide the slack is short. Oysters are in their 12th day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. Flounder are release only, the 42nd day; FF-47-2026, effective 12:01 a.m. Tuesday, is a commercial ocean trawl order and changes nothing in the sound.
